subject: Interim renewal quote + scaling credit & SLA structure
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed renewal pricing + optional mid-term uplift credits

Hi Daniel —

Attached is a refreshed proposal for Acme AI's Dedicated GPU pool renewal. Highlights: a 12-month reserved commit to match your forecasted 320 A100-equivalent units with an option to add an interim uplift at month 6 with a prepaid credit that applies toward the step-up capacity.

Key items in the attached PDF:
- Baseline commit: 320 units, sustained throughput guarantee (p99 inference latency targets) for 1.25B tokens/month
- Mid-term uplift: 20% step available at month 6 with a discounted uplift credit (prepaid) that reduces marginal rate by 18% vs list for the uplift capacity
- SLAs: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pool; separate throughput SLO with credit bands for missed targets
- Term discount tiers baked into final pricing (higher commit -> higher discount)

Two asks from our side to keep the uplift option simple:
1) agreement that uplift activation is a one-time action during month 6 window; credit is non-refundable but transferable within Acme's org
2) a short acceptance window on the quote (10 business days) so we can lock in hardware allocation for H1 2027

I'll follow up next week to run through the SLA language and throughput calculation with Hannah.

Best,
Jordan Blake

From: Daniel Park <dpark@acmeai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed renewal pricing + optional mid-term uplift credits

Jordan —

Thanks for the proposal. A few immediate questions from procurement and infra:

1) The uplift credit sounds useful, but we need clarity on unit reconciliation. If we prepay for the credit and then don’t use the uplift, is there any carryover?
2) The throughput guarantee: we run several low-latency production endpoints (short context) and some long-context research workloads. How will you attribute token consumption vs throughput SLO?
3) We need a better defined credit schedule for missed throughput SLAs — procurement is pushing for a dollar-denominated credit (not just % of monthly bill) for operational predictability.

Also, can you confirm whether the 18% uplift discount stacks with our existing enterprise commit discounts? If both apply the math needs to be explicit.

Cc’ing our lead infra contact (procurement@acmeai.com) for redlines. We’ll aim to get an initial redline back by 11/10.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Head of Procurement, Acme AI
procurement@acmeai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme questions — suggested responses + fallback

Jordan/Hannah —

Quick draft responses to Daniel's bullets. I also added a fallback commercial we can offer if procurement pushes hard: an 8-week partial credit window (instead of prepaid non-refundable) tied to actual activation of uplift capacity.

Draft answers:
- Carryover: prepaid uplift credit is not refundable; however we can offer a 6-month carry-forward on unused uplift credit if you commit to an additional 6-month extension to the term at time of uplift activation.
- Attribution: we will define two billing classes (short-context production and long-context research) with token weights and separate throughput SLO calculations. Hannah — can you draft the two-class measurement approach (calls, token weighting, monitoring hooks)?
- SLA credits: propose dollar-denominated credits tied to missed throughput bands. Example: if monthly throughput < 90% of committed tokens, credit = 5% of monthly invoice; < 80%, credit = 12% of monthly invoice. This is dollar-denominated and maps to invoice lines.
- Discount stacking: yes — uplift credit is applied to marginal uplift capacity after applying base-commit discount; we can show worked examples.

Fallback commercial: 6-week activation refund window for uplift (pro-rated) + 5% additional discount on uplift if they prepay and sign within 7 business days. Only present if procurement asks for more flexible refunds.

Jordan — propose we share the SLA draft and worked pricing examples (spreadsheet) and ask for a short call next week to walk procurement through attribution.

Marissa Cole
Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Throughput_Guarantee_SLA_Draft.docx (docx)

From: Daniel Park <dpark@acmeai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interim renewal quote + scaling credit & SLA structure

Jordan/Marissa —

Thanks for the clarifications. Procurement reviewed and has two counter requests:

1) A limited carryover is acceptable, but we need a guaranteed 3-month minimum refund window on unused uplift credit (procurement insists on an operational reserve) — can Redwood meet a 3-month refund window instead of only non-refundable credit?
2) We require clearer monitoring hooks: specific telemetry points (per-route token counters, per-pool p99 latency metrics) and a monthly SLA report PDF delivered to a named mailbox. If Redwood can provide those monitoring artifacts we can accept dollar-denominated credits.

We also need the discount stacking worked example as a simple 3-line table showing base commit, uplift capacity, and final effective rate. If you can get that to us by 11/12 we’ll target signing the amendment the week of 11/16.

Daniel Park
Head of Procurement, Acme AI

Subject: Re: Interim renewal quote + scaling credit & SLA structure

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear asks — we can accommodate both with a small commercial change. Proposed final position: 

1) Uplift credit mechanics: convert to a refundable prepaid uplift credit with a 3-month refund window for unused credit after uplift activation; if uplift never activated by month 6 the credit is refundable within the 3-month window after the option window closes. This gives Acme an operational reserve while preserving the economics.

2) Monitoring & reporting: Hannah will produce a measurement spec that includes: per-route token counters, per-pool p99 latency, aggregated token consumption by billing class, and an automated monthly SLA PDF delivered to procurement@acmeai.com. We’ll include a sample report in tomorrow's email.

3) Dollar-denominated credits: we will map SLA bands to invoice-credit percentages (worked examples attached).

4) Discount stacking: we’ll deliver a simple 3-line worked example showing base commit rate, uplift marginal rate (after base discount), and effective blended rate.

Next steps: Hannah and I will send the measurement spec + worked pricing table by EOD 11/13. If that looks good we’ll update the quote and circulate for signature (DocuSign) for amendment execution the week of 11/16.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this up.

Best,
Jordan Blake
